option_c: That you have come pleases me
option_d: If you do not hurry you will miss the train
explanation: 'That you have come' is a noun clause (subject of the verb).

question: Which of the following are complex sentences? 1. In the green vase there were four dead roses. 2. Farookh played the Sitar from 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock. 3. If it doesn't rain, we will surely come. 4. We don't know where they come from.
explanation: Sentences 3 and 4 have a dependent clause + independent clause = complex.

question: Some clauses can stand on their own as sentences and they are called ______.
explanation: Independent clauses express a complete thought and can stand alone.

question: A clause contains a ______ and a predicate of its own.
explanation: A clause contains a subject and a predicate.

question: Identify the type of clause in the brackets. (Unless it rains tomorrow), I will go to school.
explanation: 'Unless' introduces a conditional clause (means 'if not').

question: Identify the type of clause in the brackets. Our neighbour (who moved in last year) wants to borrow the chainsaw.
explanation: Relative clause giving more info about 'our neighbour', introduced by 'who'.

question: Select the most appropriate option. Dependent Clause is also called ______.
explanation: Dependent clause = subordinate clause; starts with subordinating conjunction.

question: Identify the clause in the brackets. My friend helped me (when I was in danger.)
explanation: Adverb clause of time (shows when action took place).

question: (Before it starts raining), take out your umbrella. Identify the clause in brackets.
explanation: 'Before it starts raining' is a subordinate (adverb) clause of time.

question: 'We are going to the restaurant that I love most'. The given sentence is an example of-
explanation: 'that I love most' modifies 'the restaurant' = adjective clause.

question: The vacation is (what Robert needs most) at this time. Identify the clause in the brackets.
explanation: 'what Robert needs most' is the complement of 'is' = noun clause.

question: No one spends money the way you do. Identify the underlined part (the way you do).
explanation: Adverbial clause of manner (does the work of an adverb).

question: ______ hurts me. (Choose the appropriate noun clause to replace the underlined part.)
option_d: Even the thought of his suffering
explanation: 'That you should cheat me' is the subject of 'hurts' = noun clause.

question: The stolen goods were found ______. (Choose the appropriate adverbial clause.)
option_b: where the dacoits usually hid things
option_d: and the police confiscated them all
explanation: 'where the dacoits usually hid things' acts as an adverb = adverbial clause.

question: The village ______ is now a big city. (Choose the appropriate adjective clause.)
explanation: 'where I was born' modifies 'the village' = adjective clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: The teacher told the students that their result was quite good.
explanation: Noun clause acting as direct object of 'told'.

question: Identify the underlined clause: Ram wears a shawl whereas Sham wears a coat.
explanation: 'whereas Sham wears a coat' = adverb clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: Whose car has been stolen still remains a mystery.
explanation: Noun clause acting as subject of 'remains'.

question: Identify the underlined clause: Farming depends on water, which will be available only during the monsoons.
explanation: 'which will be available...' = adjective/relative clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: I found at last the book when I had lost all hope.
explanation: 'when I had lost all hope' = adverb clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: That he may fall ill worries me.
explanation: 'That he may fall ill' contains subject + finite verb + object; principal clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: I cannot work unless there is complete calm and quiet.
explanation: 'unless there is complete calm and quiet' = adverb clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: He asked questions for which there were no answers.
explanation: 'for which there were no answers' = adjective/relative clause.

question: In the sentence "A strong wind swept through the town today", which word is the modifier and which word does it modify?
explanation: 'Strong' (adjective) modifies the noun 'wind'.

question: Leaving behind the dog was a difficult decision that the family had to take. The underlined part (Leaving behind) is-
explanation: 'Leaving behind' gives some sense but not complete = phrase.

question: The car passed by very quickly, so we could not see who was sitting inside. The underlined phrase (passed by) is-
explanation: 'passed by' = verb phrase (verb and its dependents).

question: The boy stood on the table to catch the attention of the audience. The underlined phrase (on the table) is-
explanation: 'on the table' shows place = adverbial phrase.

question: It reminded him of the house that he used to live in. The underlined part (that he used to live in) is-
explanation: Relative clause connected by 'that'.

question: His eyes caught a heap of letters. They were lying on the table. (Combine using a Relative Clause)
option_a: His eyes caught a heap of letters and were lying on the table
option_b: His eyes caught a heap of letters which were lying on the table
option_c: His eyes caught a heap of letters but were lying on the table
option_d: His eyes caught a heap of letters so that were lying on the table
explanation: Combined with relative pronoun 'which'.

question: Complete with a suitable clause: If he had asked me, ______
explanation: Conditional Type III: If + had + V3, subject + would have + V3.

question: Identify the underlined clause: They went when the morning dawned.
explanation: 'when the morning dawned' = adverb clause of time.

question: Identify the underlined clause: This is the school where I taught for six years.
explanation: Clause qualifies the noun 'school' = adjective subordinate clause.

question: Identify the underlined clause: Do they know where the road leads?
explanation: Noun clause, object of transitive verb 'know'.

question: Identify the underlined clause: I feel that she needs some guidance.
explanation: Noun subordinate clause, object of 'feel'.

question: Identify the underlined clause: The girl who is wearing a red coat is from my school.
explanation: Clause qualifies noun 'girl' = adjective subordinate clause.

question: Although they are 250 miles apart, they keep in constant contact on the internet. Which kind of sentence?
explanation: One dependent + one independent clause = complex sentence.

question: Rita loves to go to the beach and spend her days sunbathing. Which kind of sentence?
explanation: Two independent clauses = compound sentence.

question: Tom and Jerry have a big argument every summer over where they should spend their summer vacation. Which kind of sentence?
explanation: Complex sentence using adverb clause for place.

question: John dislikes sitting on the roof; he always gets a headache. Which kind of sentence?
explanation: Two independent clauses declaring complete sense separately = compound.

question: There was a time when I could lift 250 lbs. Identify the underlined clause.
explanation: 'when I could lift 250 lbs' qualifies the noun 'a time' = adjective clause.

question: Ramesh asked me where I lived. Identify the underlined clause.
explanation: 'where I lived' acts as a noun (name of place).

question: Desai is a wealthy man. Identify the underlined clause.
explanation: 'a wealthy man' qualifies the noun 'Desai' = adjective clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: Stand still, if you value your life.
explanation: 'if you value your life' functions as an adverb = adverb clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: He came in while I was out.
explanation: 'while I was out' = adverb clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: The reason why I did this is obvious.
explanation: 'why I did this' qualifies antecedent 'the reason' = adjective/relative clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: The time when the boat leaves is not fixed.
explanation: 'when the boat leaves' qualifies 'the time' = adjective clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: The reason why he took such a step is not obvious.
explanation: 'why he took such a step' qualifies antecedent 'the reason' = adjective clause.

question: Identify the clause of the underlined part: The stolen property was found in the dacoits' hiding place.
explanation: Underlined part functions as an adverb = adverb clause.

question: Which kind of sentence is the following? He confessed that he has committed the crime.
explanation: Contains a dependent clause in addition to the main clause = complex sentence.

question: Find out incorrect sentence.
option_a: But one thing, however, has not changed
option_c: If you do not work hard, you cannot succeed
option_d: I will wait here until you come back
explanation: 'But' is superfluous as 'however' already conveys the same meaning.

question: Identify the error part in the following sentence.
explanation: 'was able to help me' should replace 'were'; verb agrees with nearest subject.

question: Mark the part with the error.
explanation: 'This kind of apparel' should replace 'These kind'; singular noun required.

question: Mark the part with the error.
option_b: suggested that you be at the entrance
explanation: 'on his arrival' should replace 'on their arrival'.

question: Which part is incorrect in the given sentence?
option_a: As far as the export of wildlife is concerned
option_b: this is luckily a subject on which opinion
option_c: do not stop at political boundaries
option_d: Thinking people of Europe are just as disturbed by the depletion of Indian wildlife as we are
explanation: 'does not stop' should replace 'do not stop'; singular subject takes singular verb.

question: Which part of the following sentence is not correct? If you will eat your food, you will be allowed to play cricket.
explanation: 'If you eat' should replace 'If you will eat'; type 1 conditional.

question: If I would have / been there / I certainly would have / taken care of the problem
explanation: Conditional: 'If + past perfect' + perfect conditional. 'If I had been there...'

question: The principal of the college, together with some other teachers, are planning to organize an on-the-spot painting competition.
option_d: planning to organize an on-the-spot painting competition
explanation: With 'together with', verb agrees with first subject: 'is planning'.

question: As there are only one taxi available I have no other alternative but to pay the fare demanded by the driver.
option_a: As there are only one taxi available
explanation: Singular verb 'is' required; 'there' verb agrees with its object 'one taxi'.

question: You will either have to improve your work or I shall have to dismiss you from school.
explanation: Correlatives placement: 'Either you will have to... or I shall have to...'

question: He had been to school but he has learnt nothing there.
explanation: Subordinate clause must be past tense: 'but he had learnt nothing there'.

question: His failing to answer the question made the police suspect him.
explanation: 'His failure to answer...' — noun form fits the sense.

question: There is always danger of panic when a fire breaks up in a crowded city.
explanation: 'breaks out' should replace 'breaks up'; fire breaks out.

question: This car is superior and more costly than the one I have.
explanation: 'superior to' and 'more costly than' — both prepositions needed.

question: It is the dream of every mountaineers to climb the world's highest peak.
explanation: 'every mountaineer' — distributive adjective takes singular noun.

question: During the winter months, food and firewood were scarcely available.
explanation: 'was' should replace 'were'; two nouns as one idea take singular verb.

question: I have lost count how many times I have broken my glasses.
explanation: 'to count' should replace 'count'; verb turned to noun takes infinitive 'to'.

question: The report that covers many areas have established that situation is comic.
explanation: 'has' should replace 'have'; subject 'the report' is singular.

question: I do not want to be rude, it is simple that we have to be careful who we give this information to.
option_a: I do not want to be rude
option_c: that we have to be careful
option_d: Who we give this information to
explanation: 'whom' should replace 'who'; objective case required.

question: The roadside vendors do not know how much longer would they be able to stay.
option_d: Would they be able to stay
explanation: 'will' should replace 'would'.

question: Due to heavy rains on the area the match had to be cancelled.
explanation: 'in' should replace 'on'; heavy rains in the area.

question: Last but not the least, Ram is our most promising player.
explanation: No 'the' — 'last but not least' is a fixed idiom.

question: It is earth's magnetic field that made a compass work.
explanation: 'makes' should replace 'made'; universal truth takes present indefinite.

question: Babies do not grow at a steady rate but in steps and starts.
explanation: No error.

question: Hari is good at studies does not he? (1 good at studies, 2, 3 does not he)
explanation: 'isn't he?' should replace 'does not he?'; question tag matches sentence tense.

question: Ten miles are not a long distance
explanation: 'is' should replace 'are'; 'ten miles' treated as a whole, singular verb.

question: Although we are no longer young, we still enjoy to study languages.
explanation: 'studying' should replace 'to study'; enjoy takes gerund.

question: Before the 1920s, scientists use to think an immobilized muscle would become weaker.
explanation: 'used to' should replace 'use to'; form of habit in past.

question: Nuclear waste has traditionally been stored in steel drums what are subject to rust.
explanation: 'that' should replace 'what'.

question: The immune system is the bodies way of protecting itself against viruses.
explanation: 'body's' (singular possessive) should replace 'bodies'.

question: Originate in Ethiopia, coffee was drunk in the Arab world before it came to Europe.
explanation: 'Originated' — past participle needed to begin the sentence.

question: Amsterdam is a town who is sometimes referred to as the "Venice of Northern Europe" because of its canals.
option_a: Amsterdam is a town who is sometimes
option_b: referred to as the "Venice of Northern
explanation: 'which' should replace 'who'; non-living relative pronoun.

question: The sea wasp releases a poison that kill a person in three minutes.
explanation: 'kills' should replace 'kill'; singular subject 'a poison'.

question: Halley's comet approaches the earth, close to be visible, every seventy-five years.
explanation: 'closes' should replace 'approaches'? — book: singular verb; 'closes' should be used.

question: The two students walked besides each other in silence.
explanation: 'beside' should replace 'besides'.

question: Even though the shirt is rather expensive but I wish to purchase it with my own money.
option_a: Even though the shirt is rather expensive
option_c: purchase it with my own money.
explanation: 'But' is superfluous after 'even though'.

question: The driver was put in the prison for exceeding the speed limit.
explanation: 'in prison' should replace 'in the prison'; no 'the' required.

question: If I am you I would have seen to it that I won the prize.
option_b: I would have seen to it
explanation: 'If I were you' should replace 'If I am you'.

question: Are you lived alone or married?
explanation: 'living' should replace 'lived'; continuous tense.

question: She has told me that she saw my uncle at the fair on last Friday.
explanation: 'on' is superfluous before 'last Friday'.

question: He could not do otherwise but to obey the orders.
explanation: 'so as' should replace 'otherwise but': 'He could not do so as to obey the orders.'

question: My sister and her husband broke out when they heard the bad news.
option_c: When they heard the bad news.
explanation: 'broke down' should replace 'broke out'.

question: Without a moment's hesitation the Principal agreed to write a foreword to my book.
option_b: the Principal agreed to write a
explanation: No error.

question: I could not convince them because they persisted to suggest that I was lying.
option_a: I could not convince them because
explanation: 'persist in' should replace 'persist to'; takes gerund.

question: Most politicians are now interested in feathering their own pockets.
explanation: 'filling' should replace 'feathering'.

question: The father as well as the sons were involved in the murder.
explanation: 'was' should replace 'were'; verb agrees with 'the father' (singular).

question: He could not give cattle green fodder today because he has broken his right hand a week ago.
option_c: he has broken his right hand a week ago
explanation: 'had' should replace 'has'; past tense.

question: What to talk of charity, you do not practise even ordinary humanity.
explanation: No error.

question: I am very thirsty; give me little water to drink.
explanation: 'a little water' required; 'little' means 'not much'.

question: You and your wife appear to have seen much more happier days.
explanation: Double comparative 'much more happier' not allowed.

question: Nobody was prepared to give up their seat to the old man bending on a stick.
option_d: old man bending on a stick
explanation: 'his' should replace 'their'; 'nobody' is singular.

question: The price of this car is higher than your new car.
explanation: No error.

question: No sooner the bell rang than all students ran out of their classes helter-skelter.
explanation: 'No sooner did the bell ring' — auxiliary 'did' required after 'no sooner'.

question: The Principal, along with teacher, were invited on the occasion.
explanation: 'was' should replace 'were'; verb agrees with first subject.

question: Suresh asked Akbar when could he reach Kanpur.
explanation: 'when he could' should replace 'when could he'; indirect speech.

question: After Newton has observed an apple fall to the ground, he formulated the law of gravity.
explanation: 'had observed' should replace 'has observed'; past tense.

question: In 1740, John Newbery was the first publisher to produce books which children really wanted read.
explanation: 'to read' should replace 'read'; verb joined by infinitive 'to'.

question: The name Albert Einstein has become synonymous with his theory of relative in the minds of most scientists and laymen.
explanation: 'relativity' should replace 'relative'.

question: The most important method saving by individuals in recent years has been real estate investment, particularly in private dwellings.
explanation: 'method of savings' should replace 'method saving'.

question: The most important cause of tides is the gravitation attraction of the moon.
explanation: 'gravitational' should replace 'gravitation'.

question: One should take advantage of opportunities to talk with native orators if one wants to improve his English.
explanation: 'one's' should replace 'his'; matches 'one'.

question: The great poet and dramatist, the Kalidas, is regarded as the Shakespeare of India.
explanation: 'The' removed before proper noun unless an adjective adds value.

question: Although there are some similarities in the qualifications of the two candidates, the differences among them are quite pronounced.
explanation: 'between' should replace 'among'; two persons take 'between'.

question: He explained to the government why the manufacturing of cars have stopped in his new factory.
option_a: He explained to the government why the
option_b: manufacturing of cars have stopped in his
explanation: 'had' should replace 'have'; indirect sentence, past tense.

question: We have lived in this house ever since my father has died.
explanation: 'has' not required; last clause is past indefinite.

question: The principal claimed that there were less than fifty students present in the building when it caught fire.
option_a: The principal claimed that there were less
option_b: than fifty students present in the building
explanation: 'fewer' should replace 'less'; countable noun.

question: The examinations of the undergraduate students are likely to commence from Friday.
explanation: 'on' should replace 'from' before a day/date.

question: Few people know that the climate of Simla is better than Srinagar.
explanation: 'than that of' should follow; comparison of climates.

question: The evening came to a climax of violence when Mohan produced a box of fire-works that my cousin had sent him from Delhi and unwisely repeated a remark that Rani made earlier in the day.
explanation: 'that Rani had made' — second part is past perfect.

question: Every one of us should do our duty to the country.
explanation: 'his' should replace 'our'; 'everyone' is singular third person.

question: Neither Ram nor his parents are to blame.
explanation: Sentence is correct; verb agrees with nearer subject 'parents' (plural).

question: Very few people now believe that the wages of sin are death.
explanation: 'is' preferred; sin and death singular though 'wages' is plural.

question: Both Ram and Shyam were not present in the classroom.
explanation: 'were not present themselves' — reflexive pronoun needed with 'present'.

question: It is really strange that he has not replied my letter.
explanation: 'replied to' — 'reply' followed by 'to'.

question: Many things have happened since I have left the school.
explanation: 'since I left' — 'since' takes past tense clause.

question: He told me that he is not interested in games and sports.
explanation: 'was' should replace 'is'; reported speech in past tense.

question: The director failed in films after films which he directed.
explanation: 'film after film' — noun after noun is singular.

question: Had he reached the station a few minutes earlier he had caught the train.
explanation: 'would have caught' — conditional second clause form.

question: He committed suicide twice before he died and left the members of his family crying.
option_d: the members of his family crying
explanation: No error.

question: We congratulated him for winning a scholarship and being awarded the Governor's medal.
option_c: and being awarded the Governor's medal
explanation: 'on winning' should replace 'for winning'.

question: The furnitures purchased by me is sub-standard and not fit for my drawing room.
option_c: not fit for my drawing room
explanation: 'The furniture' — uncountable noun takes no 's'.

question: Unemployment is a very actual problem. (1 Unemployment is, 2 a, 3 very, 4 actual problem)
explanation: 'prominent' should replace 'actual'.

question: I would request you to see my cousin sister who has just returned from Germany.
explanation: 'would' not required in option (a).

question: Can I lend your pencil for a minute please?
explanation: 'Could/Would' should replace 'Can'; polite request.

question: A lot of travel delay is caused due to inefficiency and lack of good management on behalf of the railways.
option_a: A lot of travel delay is caused
option_b: due to inefficiency and lack of good management
explanation: 'a great deal of' should replace 'a lot of'.

question: Neelima has scored a first class in her final exams, is not it?
option_a: Neelima has scored a first class
explanation: 'hasn't she?' should replace 'is not it?'; question tag matches verb.

question: The conductor asked the passenger why had not he purchased a ticket in advance to board the bus.
option_a: The conductor asked the passenger why had not
explanation: 'why he had not' should replace 'why had not he'; indirect interrogative.

question: It is unfortunate that many youngsters get addicted to gamble.
explanation: 'gambling' should replace 'gamble'; addicted to + gerund.

question: Roses grow with abundance against this old wall in this season.
explanation: 'in abundance' should replace 'with abundance'.

question: It is possible to multiply this bacteria in the laboratory.
explanation: 'these' should replace 'this'; 'bacteria' is plural.

question: Even though the shirt is rather expensive but I wish to purchase it.
option_d: but I wish to purchase it
explanation: 'yet' should replace 'but' after 'even though'.

question: When was Arnold's essay "The Function of Criticism at the Present Time" published?
explanation: Published 1865; influential critical essay on the critic's role.

question: Who made the observation about Shelley that he is "a beautiful and ineffectual angel, beating in the void his luminous wings in vain"?
explanation: Arnold on Shelley — "beautiful and ineffectual angel".

question: Who highlighted the importance of poetry in the manner: "More and more mankind will discover that they have to turn to poetry to interpret life for us, to consol, to sustain us. explanation: Arnold on poetry replacing religion/philosophy (Study of Poetry).

question: In which landscape is "The Scholar Gipsy" imagined?
explanation: The Scholar Gipsy set in Oxfordshire pastoral landscape.

question: Who among the following has said about Milton that "he is our first great artist in style, our first rate master in grand style"?

question: In "The Function of Criticism at the Present Time" what is proposed by Matthew Arnold as the essence of criticism?
explanation: Disinterestedness = essence of criticism.

question: Who, in "The World as India," argues that English can be the only common "unifying language" of India?
explanation: Susan Sontag, "The World as India".

explanation: Personal & Historic estimate = fallacious estimates.

question: Which Shakespearean comedy is structured as a play within a play?

question: Who has written "Culture and Anarchy"?
explanation: Culture and Anarchy by Matthew Arnold (1869).

explanation: Hinkseys/Sibylla/Ilsley Downs appear in Thyrsis.

explanation: Lines from Rugby Chapel.

explanation: Thyrsis commemorates Arthur Hugh Clough.

question: Matthew Arnold is known as ______.

explanation: Arnold worked as a school inspector.

question: Which of the following does not mention 'Dover Beach'?

question: Matthew Arnold's 'Memorial Verses' mourns the death of ..........

question: How does Dover Beach treat the 'sea'?
option_a: The sea shifts from being an object to an image, from a visual object to an aural s.......

option_d: The sea, an inanimate object, is personified and sadness, a typical human feeling

question: Who is the author of the poem 'Sohrab and Rustum'?
explanation: Sohrab and Rustum by Matthew Arnold (1853).

question: 'The Touchstone method' of literary criticism has been propounded by
explanation: Touchstone method propounded by Arnold.

question: "Poetry is simply the most delightful and perfect form of utterance that human words can reach." The above definition has been given by
explanation: Definition given by Matthew Arnold.

question: The reference of "faithful shepherd" appears in which of the following poems?
explanation: "Faithful shepherd" appears in Rugby Chapel.

question: About whom did Arnold write in his poem 'Memorial verses'-'He laid us as we lay at birth/on the cool flowery lap of birth...'?
explanation: Memorial Verses about Wordsworth.

question: What is the name of Greek tragedy written by Matthew Arnold?
explanation: Greek tragedy Merope (1858).

question: "Thyrsis" was written by Arnold to commemorate his friend Arthur Hugh Clough who had died in 1861 at the age of
explanation: Clough died aged 42.

question: ".... for the world which seems to lie before us like a land of dreams." is taken from a poem by
explanation: Line from Dover Beach (Arnold).

question: The Greek playwright who is referred to in Dover Beach:

question: Who introduced the concept of Touchstone in literary criticism?
explanation: Touchstone concept introduced by Arnold.

question: 'Poetry is a criticism of life under the conditions fixed for such a criticism by laws of poetic truth and poetic beauty.' Who among the following, made the above statement?

question: "Rugby Chapel" is a poem by Matthew Arnold in the memory of his:
explanation: Rugby Chapel in memory of his father.

question: The famous line "... where ignorant armies clash by night" is taken from a poem by:
explanation: "Ignorant armies clash by night" — Dover Beach (Arnold).

question: "The future of poetry is immense, because in poetry..... our race, as time goes on, will find an ever surer and surer stay."-This claim for poetry is made in:
explanation: Claim made in Arnold's The Study of Poetry.

question: According to Matthew Arnold, 'touchstones' help us test truth and seriousness that constitute the best poetry. What are the 'touchstones'?
option_a: The purple passages of lyric poetry
option_c: The lines and expressions of the great masters
option_d: Passages of epic strength and vigour

question: "No, no thou hast not felt the lapse of hours! For what wears out the life of mortal men? 'Tis that repeated shocks, again, again, Exhaust the energy of strongest souls And numb the elastic powers..." Who does the poet address here?
explanation: Poet addresses The Scholar Gipsy.

question: "All great literature is, at bottom, a criticism of life"-this statement is attributed to:
explanation: Attributed to Matthew Arnold.

question: Matthew Arnold's "touchstones" were short passages... In his "Study of Poetry" Arnold cited "touchstones" from Homer and Dante and also from the English poets Shakespeare and Milton. Which English poet did he disapprovingly call "not one of the great classics" in the list below?
explanation: Arnold called Chaucer "not one of the great classics".

question: The Elegy written by Matthew Arnold on the death of Arthur Clough is
explanation: Elegy on Clough = Thyrsis.

question: "Poetry, at bottom, is a criticism of life", was said by
explanation: Said by Matthew Arnold.

question: Arnold was the first English critic to stress upon the necessity of
explanation: Arnold stressed comparative criticism.

question: Which of the following poets wrote the poem entitled 'Dover Beach'?
explanation: Dover Beach written by Arnold.

question: In which category will you place Arnold as a critic?
explanation: Arnold placed in classicist category.

question: Who regarded poetry as the criticism of life?
explanation: Arnold regarded poetry as criticism of life.

question: Matthew Arnold studied at ----- University.
explanation: Arnold studied at Oxford (Balliol College).

question: The best poems of Matthew Arnold are
explanation: Best poems of Arnold = elegies.

question: Matthew Arnold as a poet was most influenced by
explanation: Arnold most influenced by Wordsworth.

question: "this strange disease of modern life, with its sick hurry and divided aim", Mathew Arnold speaks of this malaise in his poem.
explanation: Malaise spoken of in The Scholar Gypsy.

question: Who termed Shelley as 'Melopoeic'?
explanation: Arnold termed Shelley "Melopoeic".

question: Arnold took the theme of his 'The Scholar Gipsy' from Joseph Glanville's book entitled-
explanation: Theme from Glanville's The Vanity of Dogmatizing.

question: Who is referred as 'Europe's sagest head' and 'Physician of the iron age' by Arnold.
explanation: Goethe = Europe's sagest head / physician of the iron age.

question: Who was the father of Matthew Arnold?
explanation: Father = Thomas Arnold.

question: Whose death was commemorated by Arnold in Thyrsis?
explanation: Thyrsis commemorates Arthur Hugh Clough.

question: Arnold's celebrated 'The Scholar Gipsy' is based on an old legend, narrated by Glanville in
explanation: Based on legend in The Vanity of Dogmatizing.

question: Who is the author of the poem 'Shakespeare'?
explanation: Poem Shakespeare by Matthew Arnold.

question: Mathew Arnold's "Sohrab and Rustum" is taken from a story from:
explanation: Theme from Shah Namah (Ferdowsi).

question: Which of these is not a poem by Mathew Arnold?
explanation: The King's Tragedy is by D.G. Rossetti, not Arnold.

question: In Matthew Arnold's 'Culture and Anarchy' the term 'Philistines' is used for:
explanation: Philistines = English middle class.

question: Who wrote Sohrab and Rustum?
explanation: Sohrab and Rustum by Mathew Arnold.

question: Who praised Shakespeare thus? "Others abide our question thou art free We ask and ask – Thou smilest and art still"
explanation: Praised by Matthew Arnold ("On Shakespeare").

question: Matthew Arnold's Rugby Chapel commemorates:
explanation: Rugby Chapel commemorates his father Thomas.

question: Who is 'Thyrsis' in the poem of the same name?
explanation: Thyrsis = Arthur Hugh Clough.

question: Which of the following works is not associated with Matthew Arnold?
explanation: Culture and Environment not by Arnold (Chemers & Altman).

question: Matthew Arnold was not a/an
explanation: Arnold was not an essayist (per key).

question: "Is there no life, but these alone? Madman or slave, must man be one?" The above lines are from
explanation: Lines from A Summer Night.

question: Rugby Chapel by Matthew Arnold is written in the memory of
explanation: Rugby Chapel in memory of Thomas Arnold.

question: "He laid us as we lay at birth On the Cool flowery lap of earth." In the above lines 'He' stands for
explanation: 'He' = Wordsworth (Memorial Verses).

question: "Others abide our question, thou art free", 'Thou' stands for
explanation: 'Thou' = Shakespeare.

question: Who is the Author of Culture and Anarchy?
explanation: Culture and Anarchy by Matthew Arnold.

question: "The Function of Criticism at the Present Time" was written by
explanation: Written by M. Arnold (1865).

question: Arnold's ..................... ushers in Persian history:
explanation: Sohrab and Rustum ushers in Persian history.

question: Which of the following characteristics describes the tone of Dover Beach best?
explanation: Tone of Dover Beach = pessimistic.

question: Matthew Arnold wrote .......... which is a great exposition on culture:
explanation: Culture and Anarchy = exposition on culture.

question: Arnold's Empedocles on Etna is a/an:
explanation: Empedocles on Etna = dramatic/melodramatic poem.

question: In which poem does Matthew Arnold express the dilemma of: "Wandering between two worlds, one dead, The other powerless to be born"?
explanation: Dilemma expressed in Stanzas from the Grande Chartreuse.

question: Which of the following statements about Samson Agonistes is incorrect?
option_a: This is the first work of Milton.
option_b: It deals with the last part of Samson's life.
option_c: The play opens with Samson blind and prisoner of the philistines.
option_d: In the end he kills himself and the philistine by pulling down the pillars of the structure in which they were sitting.
explanation: Samson Agonistes (1671) is a closet tragedy on Samson's final phase; it was not Milton's first work.

question: The name 'Lycidas' is taken from which of the following Greek Poets?
explanation: Lycidas (1638), a pastoral elegy, takes its name from the Greek poet Theocritus.

question: Who among the following writers is the author of "Doctrine and Discipline of Divorce"?
explanation: Milton's prose tract 'The Doctrine and Discipline of Divorce' was first published in 1643.

question: Which poet influenced Keats's "The Fall of Hyperion" (1819)?
explanation: Milton influenced Keats's 'The Fall of Hyperion'; its style recalls Paradise Lost.

question: Which of the following poems has NOT been composed by Milton?
explanation: Hydrotaphia (Urn Burial) is by Sir Thomas Browne (1658), not Milton.

question: In which book of Paradise Lost does Milton refer to "Agra and Lahore of Great Mogul"?
explanation: In Book XI Milton refers to 'Agra and Lahore of Great Mogul' (Lahore at its Mughal peak).

question: A postmodern parody of "A Valediction Forbidding Mourning" was written with the same title by ___.
explanation: Adrienne Rich reused the title of Donne's poem for a postmodern parody.

question: Milton in his Paradise Lost, Book I has written: "And justifie the ways of God to man." What is the subject of the verb "justifie" in the text of the poem?
explanation: The subject of 'justifie' is 'I' — the poet stating his purpose to justify God's ways to men.

question: "Milton was of the devil's party without knowing it." Who made the above statement?
explanation: William Blake made this remark, implying Milton unconsciously glorified Satan in Book I.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly Matched?
option_a: Ode to the West Wind - Terza rima
explanation: 'On His Blindness' is an Italian sonnet in iambic pentameter, not a heroic quatrain.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct with reference to Milton's poetry? (1) It combines two conflicting cultures-humanism/and puritanism. (2) It sublime both in though and style. (3) It is totally objective and full of humour. (4) It is written in rhyme royal.
explanation: Milton's poetry is not wholly objective/humorous, and most of his work is blank verse, not rhyme royal.

question: "Lap me in soft Lydian airs, Married to immortal verse Such as the meeting soul may pierce In notes, with many a winding bout." The above lines appear in
explanation: These lines appear in L'Allegro (1631), which portrays the cheerful man's pleasures.

question: Milton's 'On Shakespeare' was published in
explanation: 'On Shakespeare' (sonnet) was published in 1630 — Milton's first published poem in English.

question: The line 'They also serve who only stand and wait' occurs in which of the following poems?
option_d: 'Ode on a Grecian Urn' by John Keats
explanation: The line closes 'On His Blindness', Milton's sonnet on his loss of sight (c.1652).

question: Which of the following forms does Satan not take in 'Paradise Lost'?
explanation: Satan takes the forms of cherub, cormorant, toad, and snake — never an owl.

question: 'Paradise Lost', is written in ____ verse.
explanation: Paradise Lost is in blank verse (unrhymed iambic pentameter), over 10,000 lines.

question: Who guards the gates of Hell in Milton's 'Paradise Lost'?
explanation: Sin, Satan's daughter, guards the gates of Hell (with Death).

question: 'Lycidas', by John Milton is an ____.
explanation: Lycidas is a pastoral elegy (monody) lamenting Edward King's death (1637).

question: John Milton's 'Areopagitica' was about the freedom of ____.
explanation: Areopagitica (1644) argues for freedom of speech and unlicensed printing.

question: Which of the following is not a work of John Milton?
explanation: 'Venus and Adonis' (1593) is Shakespeare's narrative poem, not Milton's.

question: How many books does "Paradise Regained" consist of?
explanation: Paradise Regained (1671) is a poem in four books.

question: In which year John Milton was born?
explanation: Milton was born 9 December 1608 in Bread Street, London.

question: Which poet made illustrations for "Il Penseroso"?
explanation: William Blake made illustrations for 'Il Penseroso'.

question: Which text of Milton does the following line appear in, "Thou canst not touch the freedom of my mind"?
explanation: The line appears in Comus, a masque in honour of chastity.

question: John Milton studied at:
explanation: Milton studied at Christ's College, Cambridge University.

question: The famous epic Paradise Lost by Milton contains
explanation: Paradise Lost contains 12 books (10 in 1667; rearranged to 12 in 1674).

question: Which of the following poems is not composed by John Milton?
explanation: 'True Love' is by Shakespeare (sonnet 116); the others are Milton's.

question: Who is at once the child of the Renaissance and the Reformation?
explanation: Milton is called the child of the Renaissance and the Reformation.

question: Which one of the following is a Pastoral elegy written by Milton?
option_c: Elegy Written in A Country Church Yard
option_d: Elegy to the Memory of an Unfortunate Lady
explanation: Lycidas (1637) is a pastoral elegy on Edward King's death.

question: Who of the following was the first to suggest that Satan is the real hero of Paradise Lost?
explanation: William Blake first suggested Satan is the real hero of Paradise Lost.

question: Milton composed Areopagitica in ____.
explanation: Areopagitica (1644) is a prose speech for the liberty of unlicensed printing.

question: What impelled Milton the Puritan to employ the 'masque' and compose Comus?
option_a: To re-usher in 'masquing' into a Puritan society.
option_b: To emphasize the virtue (of an individual) over debauchery (in the court).
option_c: To showcase his artistic abilities as a dramatist.
option_d: To celebrate the elevation of an earl to a lord.
explanation: Comus (1634), a masque, emphasizes virtue over courtly debauchery.

question: Which epic convention that Milton followed in Paradise Lost is missing in this list? (Noble theme, invocation to Muse, deployment of heroic figures, beginning in the middle, elevated style, catalogues, war-like speeches, supernatural machinery, allusions.)
explanation: 'Unity of action' is the epic convention missing from the given list.

question: Study the lines from Milton's sonnet addressed to the nightingale: 'Now timely sing, ere the rude bird of hate / Foretell my hopeless doom in some grove nigh.' What is the 'rude bird of hate' referred to here?
explanation: The 'rude bird of hate' is the Cuckoo, contrasted with the Nightingale of love.

question: A crucial aspect of Milton's divergence from the Petrarchan sonnet tradition concerns not on employed or the 'occasional' nature of his sonnets, but also ____.
option_a: the presence of a slight pause at the end of the fourth line
option_b: how the thought rhythm of the octave carried on into the sestet without any break
option_c: the rejection of the idyllic love-poetry traditions of the Elizabethans
option_d: the rejection of the three quatrains and the couplet scheme of Shakespeare
explanation: Milton diverged by rejecting the idyllic love-poetry traditions of the Elizabethans.

question: In which work, Milton states that - "While the still Morn went out with sandals grey"?
explanation: The line appears in Lycidas (1637), the pastoral elegy for Edward King.

question: Through which work does Milton intend, 'to justify the ways of God to men'?
explanation: Paradise Lost is where Milton intends to 'justify the ways of God to men'.

question: In which work of John Milton does the character 'Delilah' appear?
explanation: Delilah, Samson's wife, appears in Samson Agonistes (1671).

question: In the opening invocation of the Paradise Lost 'Oreb' refers to
explanation: 'Oreb' refers to Mount Horeb, where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments.

question: In the state of his blindness, with whom Milton does not compare himself?
explanation: Milton compares himself to Thamyris, Maeonides, Tiresias and Phineus — not Lycidas.

question: Who is often called as 'The Political Son of Spenser'?
explanation: Dryden called Milton the 'Poetical Son of Spenser'.

question: Which of the following is mismatched with reference to John Milton's work?
explanation: Areopagitica was published in 1644, not 1647.

question: Which of the following is a 'pastoral elegy'?
option_a: Elegy written in a Country Churchyard
explanation: Lycidas (1637) is a pastoral elegy, a form originated by Theocritus.

question: Milton's Paradise Regained takes its theme from
explanation: Paradise Regained takes its theme from St. Luke's Gospel.

question: Who remarked about his father as given below: "My father destined me from my infancy to the study of polite literature, which I embraced with such avidity, that from the age of twelve, I hardly ever retired from my books before midnight."
explanation: Milton remarked this about his father (Diaches, Critical History of English Literature).

question: Which of the following works is not written by John Milton?
option_d: Alma or the Progress of the Mind
explanation: 'Alma or the Progress of the Mind' is by Matthew Prior, not Milton.

question: Which of the following works is not written by John Milton?
option_b: On the Late Massacre of Piedmont
option_c: Ode on the Morning of Christ's Nativity
explanation: 'The Passionate Pilgrim' (attributed to Shakespeare) is not Milton's work.

question: Which of the following statements is true about Milton's sonnet 'On His Blindness'?
option_a: 'On His Blindness' is a precursor to 'Lycidas'
option_b: 'On His Blindness' is a curtel sonnet
option_c: Milton did not give a title to his sonnet. The title 'On His Blindness' is given by later anthologists.
explanation: Milton gave no title; 'On His Blindness' was assigned by Thomas Newton in 1761.

question: Which of the following statements is incorrect with reference to John Milton?
option_a: In 1671, Milton issued his last volume of poetry, which contained Paradise Regained and 'Samson Agonistes'
option_b: Paradise Regained is briefer and poorer than Paradise Lost
option_c: 'Samson Agonistes', in form, has no unity of time, place and action
option_d: 'Lycidas' has the colour and music of the best Spenserian verse
explanation: Incorrect: Samson Agonistes in fact observes the unities of time, place and action.

question: How, according to Milton in his "On His Blindness", does one best serve God?
option_b: by submitting to his will quietly
explanation: One best serves God by submitting quietly to His will.

question: Milton's first work is
option_b: On the Morning of Christ's Nativity
explanation: Milton's first work is 'On the Morning of Christ's Nativity' (1629).

question: John Milton's 'Lycidas' and Matthew Arnold's 'Thyrsis' are examples of ____
explanation: Both are pastoral elegies — Lycidas for Edward King, Thyrsis for A. H. Clough.

question: Which of the following poems did Milton write in Octosyllabic Couplets?
option_c: On the Late Massacre in Piedmont
explanation: Il Penseroso (1631) is written in rhymed octosyllabic couplets.

question: The phrase, 'bottomless perdition' occurs in Milton's 'Paradise Lost' in:
explanation: 'Bottomless perdition' appears in Book I, line 47 of Paradise Lost.

question: It appears that in Paradise Lost Book I 'Milton belongs to the Devil's party without knowing it'. Who among the following made this statement?
explanation: William Blake observed that Milton belonged to the Devil's party unknowingly.

question: What is 'L'Allegro's' companion piece called?
explanation: L'Allegro (the happy man) is paired with Il Penseroso (the melancholy man).

question: Identify the correctly matched group: i. 'L'Allegro and Il Penseroso' ii. 'Lycidas' iii. 'Comus' iv. 'On His Blindness' v. 'Areopagitica' with 1.pastoral elegy 2.masque 3.Sonnet 4.Prose tract 5.Companion poems in octo-syllabic couplets
explanation: Correct: i-5 (companion poems), ii-1 (pastoral elegy), iii-2 (masque), iv-3 (sonnet), v-4 (prose tract).

question: In 'Paradise Lost', Milton invokes his 'Heavenly Muse', 'Urania' at the beginning of: I.Book one II.Book four III.Book nine IV.Book seven. The right combination is
explanation: Milton invokes Urania at the start of Book One and Book Seven.

question: Which of the following works of John Milton is an elegy?
explanation: Lycidas (1637, pub. 1638) is Milton's pastoral elegy.

question: In Paradise Lost Book IX Milton writes that Adam was overcome with "____" and so ate the forbidden fruit against his "better knowledge".
explanation: Adam was overcome with 'female charm' and ate the fruit against his better knowledge.

question: "That glory never shall his wrath or might extort from me." (Paradise Lost, Book I) What 'glory' is being referred to by Satan?
option_a: The courage never to submit or yield
explanation: Satan refers to the glory of the courage never to submit or yield.

question: Which of the following statement is NOT true of Areopagitica?
option_b: It argues for the liberty of Unlicensed Printing.
option_c: It pleads for British privileges regarding Free Trade.
option_d: It is speech addressed to the Parliament of England.
explanation: Not true: Areopagitica argues for unlicensed printing, not free-trade privileges.

question: In tracing the History of English poetry, Thomas Gray's "Progress of Poesy" invokes a major poet as follows: "Nor second He, that rode sublime / Upon the seraph-wings of Extasy, / The secrets of th' Abyss to spy." Who is "He"?
explanation: Gray refers to John Milton in 'The Progress of Poesy'.

question: Who among the following was a contemporary of John Milton and wrote The Worthy Communicant? It is said that his prose "can be read easily, when Milton's must be studied."
explanation: Jeremy Taylor, Milton's contemporary, wrote 'The Worthy Communicant' (1660).

question: The opening sixteen lines of Paradise Lost comprise:
explanation: The first 16 lines of Paradise Lost comprise a single sentence.

question: In Paradise Lost Milton presents the action of the fall of man in two stages in Books ____.
explanation: The Fall of Man is presented in two stages, in Books IV and IX.

question: "Where there is leisure for fiction, there is little grief", was Samuel Johnson's criticism of a famous poem. Which poem was it?
option_c: Thomas Gray's "Elegy Written on a Country Churchyard"
explanation: Johnson criticised Milton's Lycidas thus in his 'Lives of Poets' (1779).

question: As Adam and Eve leave Paradise, "hand in hand with wandring steps and slow" (Book XII, Paradise Lost) what is their consolation?
option_a: They are comforted by their love for one another
option_b: They are comforted by their foreknowledge of the coming of Christ as Redeemer of mankind
option_c: They are comforted by God, who travels before them in the form of a pillar of fire
option_d: They are comforted by the angel, who holds each of them by the hand
explanation: Their consolation is foreknowledge of Christ as Redeemer of mankind.

question: In 'Paradise Lost' which character narrates the story of the making of Eve from a rib in Adam's side?
explanation: Adam himself tells the story of Eve's making in Book VIII.

question: John Milton's description of gold as a "precious bane" (Paradise Lost, Book II) is best described as
explanation: 'Precious bane' is an oxymoron — valuable yet distressing.

question: Milton's lament for his blindness occurs in-
explanation: Milton laments his blindness in the Nativity Ode (per the source).

question: Who replies to Milton's question "Doth God exact day-labour, light denied" in "On His Blindness"?
explanation: 'Patience' replies to Milton's question in On His Blindness.

question: Milton's 'On His Blindness' ends with an expression of the poet's
option_b: Questioning of the Justice of God
option_d: Resentment at the loss of his talent
explanation: The sonnet ends expressing the poet's faith in God's way.

question: Who is Milton's 'On His Blindness' is believed to serve God best?
option_a: One who bears his burden best
option_b: One who presents a true account of his talent
option_c: One who doesn't allow talent to become useless
option_d: One who makes full use of his talent
explanation: One who bears his burden best is believed to serve God best.

question: Milton's "On His Blindness" is:
explanation: 'On His Blindness' is a Petrarchan sonnet (octave + sestet with caesura).

question: "They also serve who only stand and wait". In this line from "On His Blindness" 'they' stands for those who:
option_c: patiently accept the decree of God
option_d: make use of their poetic talent
explanation: 'They' stands for those who patiently accept the decree of God.

question: In line 3 of his "On His Blindness" Milton speaks of 'one talent'. What is it?
explanation: 'One talent which is death to hide' refers to his poetic ability.

question: Who is the writer of "Essays on Milton"?
explanation: Macaulay's essay 'Milton' (Edinburgh Review, 1825).

question: "They also serve who only stand and wait" From which poem has this line been taken?
explanation: The line is from Milton's 'On His Blindness' (1673).

question: "When I consider how my light is spent." What does "light" refer to
explanation: 'Light' refers to Milton's failing eyesight.

question: John Milton was blinded in the year 1652, what other event is peculiar in the year.
